Not a duplicate of closed #6469 (that was an AddComponentPool NRE fixed by #6482), and a different cause from #10456. The Sentry event shows ComputeBuffer.SetData hitting a disposed bones buffer. Sequence: InstantiateExistingAvatar calls ReleaseAvatar.Execute (which disposes the skinning buffers) before it rebuilds. The rebuild then throws (UNITY-EXPLORER-NQ8 / #7809, here an NRE on get_gameObject inside AttachmentAssetUtility.InstantiateOrGetCached; likely cause: line 60 calls DestroyImmediate on a parent MeshRenderer's GameObject, then reads .gameObject of a nested MeshRenderer that is already destroyed). That leaves the entity with a disposed AvatarCustomSkinningComponent while IsDirty stays true, so it retries every frame. Fixing the cascade means making the avatar rebuild transactional and ending the retry loop, which is a design change and the same one the W36 sweep skipped under #9985. No fix is on dev or in an open PR (#10083 skips #9985).

design change across the native Rust Segment queue and startup: every instance shares persistentDataPath/analytics_queue_v1.sqlite3 and Segment starts before the single-instance check, and nothing repairs a corrupt DB; needs a native rebuild (recreate on DatabaseCorrupt) and/or a per-instance queue file

design change across modules: skinning (ComputeSkinningBufferContainer), spring bones (AttachmentAssetUtility.BuildSpringBoneData, SpringBoneRegistrationSystem) and reused instances all assume joint index == base bone index; a skinning-only remap leaves spring bones broken, and it needs the reporter's GLBs plus an avatar-rendering owner
